reason: Changes only .github/workflows/package.yml to retry packaging after transient notarization failures. This is package-production maintenance, not a change to shipped application behavior.
Moves layout ownership into Components while retaining the serialized representation. This internal preparation does not change layout cleanup behavior.

Allows the remaining group to replace an outer layout after a window closes. The supplied 0.2.18 base explicitly skips cleanup of nonempty roots in layout_tree.rs:1057–1081, establishing a shipped limitation. Head retains the fix and regression tests; scroll layouts remain exempt.

Replaces recursive promotion with a loop and clarifies comments. The recursion was introduced by the preceding unreleased implementation and is absent from the released base; there is no separate user-facing outcome.

The merge confirms the net root-cleanup fix and regression tests. Supporting ownership, orientation, and tree-operation changes are grouped into the same outcome; comparison with the base's root exemption establishes the release boundary.

Removes the mouse-delta resize path and follows application resize notifications instead. The supplied 0.2.18 base contains both paths and uses a listen-only mouse tap, supporting a shipped double-application problem and the correction to respect application size constraints.
Adds resize-edge hit-test coverage, including narrow windows, without changing production behavior.

Guards a direct viewport update introduced by this group's new resize-completion helper. Both the update and guard are removed before release; the helper was absent from the base. This is an unreleased-only intermediate fix.

Lets the final resize notification update the viewport. Base reactor.rs:690–706 suppresses viewport updates for size changes, while base layout.rs:1528–1538 recenters through mouse-driven completion, establishing that the final-notification problem predates this work. The regression test verifies that the widened column becomes visible after resizing.

Redundant aggregate attribution: the merge verifies the resizing changes and tests already represented by the component commits. Head glide.default.toml:233–237 confirms that scroll layout remains experimental and disabled by default.
Introduces an internal event-tap wrapper with callback ownership and run-loop cleanup. It supports later work but provides no independently useful user capability.

Migrates mouse APIs while preserving event subscriptions and dispatch, adjusts a diagnostic click monitor, and adds teardown cleanup. No separate end-user outcome is established; the later recovery fix is checked against the pre-migration base.
Replaces integer error comparisons with CGError::Success and updates the error type while preserving success and error branches. No user-facing behavior change is established.
Migrates the diagnostic focus watcher's run-loop API and converts its existing polling interval. This is developer-tool maintenance.
Removes three legacy dependencies after migrating their callers. No user-facing compatibility requirement, default, or performance effect is established.
The merge confirms equivalent event forwarding and cursor success checks during the API migration. Its wrapper and dependency changes have no independent release-note outcome.

Adds recovery for system-disabled event taps. Head event_tap.rs:290–312 re-enables monitoring when intended, and the mouse actor uses the wrapper. The supplied 0.2.18 base enables its mouse tap once and has no disabled-tap recovery branch, establishing a shipped problem rather than a wrapper regression.

The merge verifies recovery and the guard preserving intentional disables; head retains both. Grouped with the implementation as one mouse-monitoring outcome. Claims about improved keyboard-tap reliability remain separately unresolved.
Updates only the documentation site's lockfile for postcss-selector-parser and removes cssesc. The site manifest is unchanged, and no application or published-site behavior change is demonstrated.
The merge contains the same documentation-site lockfile update and no additional changes. Upstream security claims do not establish a shipped Glide issue requiring release notes.
Adds a manually triggered release-note evaluation workflow that is absent from the base. This is repository automation, not an application capability.
Adds caching and version verification and updates the release-scribe pin. These refine automation introduced in this range without changing Glide behavior.
Expands release-note editorial guidelines and examples. This is contributor guidance, not documentation of a new application capability.
Changes only the pinned release-scribe revision. No effect on Glide users is demonstrated.
Replaces release-tool checkout, build, and cache steps with cargo-install. This changes repository automation installation, not Glide installation.
Adds the release-notes environment and updates the tool pin. This scopes automation credentials and execution rather than application permissions.
The merge contains release-scribe configuration, its workflow, and contributor/editorial guidance. The workflow is absent from the base, and no user-facing Glide outcome is established.

Sets an automation input budget, updates the tool pin, and adds a preflight workflow. The preflight is deleted before release, and the intermediate budget is later increased; none changes the application.
Updates the evaluation tool pin and deletes the preflight workflow introduced earlier in this range. These are internal automation changes.
Raises release-scribe max_input_bytes from 2,000,000 to 4,000,000. This is an evidence budget for note generation, not a Glide runtime limit or user setting.
The merge changes only the release-scribe input budget and evaluation tool pin. Head confirms the final values; there is no user-facing application outcome.
Exposes an internal handler and adds test-only screen-space mocks while preserving production screen filtering. This supports tests rather than changing released behavior.
Adds a simulated macOS environment beneath the test-only testing module. The scenarios do not establish a production fix.
Adds Scene rendering and assertions for tests. Its final module is test-only, so its diagrams are developer tooling rather than a new layout capability.
Adds screen fixtures that construct reactor test events. Shipped display configuration and defaults do not change.
Replaces layout-tree test frame assertions and hand-drawn comments with Scene snapshots. No production balancing or layout behavior change is established.
Changes layout-manager test helpers and assertions inside a cfg(test) module. The depicted layouts are expectations, not newly available features.
Replaces reactor test frame comparisons with fills_screen assertions without changing how users' windows are resized.
Changes assertion failure wording in the test-only Scene implementation. It is not an application diagnostic or sizing fix.
Migrates simulated scenarios to Scene relations and drawings. These test-only assertions do not demonstrate a production behavior change.
Moves Scene and simulator support into a testing module declared under cfg(test) in head src/lib.rs. This is test organization only.
Adds pixel-difference resize assertions to test-only Scene support. It does not add a production resize command or change window sizing.
Wires real actors to simulated app, controller, and Dock components in test-only support. More faithful simulation and exposed failures are not themselves production fixes.
Documents layout assertions and snapshot updates for contributors. There is no corresponding application capability or user adoption requirement.

Described as documenting a Mission Control limitation in the simulator, but its patch and affected lines were not collected. The final test-only module suggests exclusion, but the precise change and any production effect remain unverified.

The inspected merge adds test infrastructure, assertion migrations, contributor guidance, internal handler visibility, and test-gated mocks. Head confirms the testing module is cfg(test). No merge-level user outcome is supported; the uninspected follow-up remains separately unresolved.

Prevents windows without an assigned Space from being tiled during Mission Control. The regression test verifies that a newly opened window does not trigger a switch on exit. The permissive fallback exists in base reactor.rs:1194–1204, establishing a shipped problem; head retains the correction.
Changes only simulated accessibility window enumeration to reflect the shown desktop. This improves test fidelity rather than runtime behavior.
Extracts the existing per-app layout update into a helper while retaining discovery and focus updates. It supports the fix without adding an independent user outcome.

Refreshes window membership before raising windows when Mission Control closes. A simulation test verifies no desktop switch after dragging the focused window away. Base reactor.rs:790–809 raises the old layout without refreshing, establishing that the problem predates this range; head retains the fix.

Redundant aggregate attribution: the merge combines the two Mission Control corrections already represented by their implementation commits, plus supporting refactoring and tests. Both corrections remain in head.

Adds discovery after unlocking and when an unknown app activates. The supplied 0.2.18 base discovers apps only at startup and through launch notifications, establishing a released gap. Head wm_controller.rs:189–207 and 277–300 retains both recovery paths.

The merge confirms the same app-discovery correction and is grouped into one outcome. No retries after app-thread initialization failures are claimed; that discussion is not implemented by the inspected patch.

Introduces Glide-owned hotkey parsing, replacing livesplit_hotkey::Hotkey used by the 0.2.18 base. The parser refactor needs no standalone entry, but reported rejection of formerly accepted key names may require migration guidance. The complete old/new accepted-name comparison is missing.

Adds Cmd and Command aliases to the new parser. Base documentation already lists Cmd, but base behavior depends on livesplit-hotkey 0.8.1. Its parser must be inspected before classifying this as a shipped documentation mismatch or an unreleased parser regression.
Adds an active event-tap API and pass/consume dispositions. This is infrastructure for side-specific shortcuts, not a separate capability or established shipped fix.

Switches shortcut registration to the replacement manager. The replacement is internal, but a claimed timeout-recovery improvement needs comparison of the new keyboard tap and the released livesplit-hotkey implementation. The supplied code does not establish both recovery paths.

Introduces separate left/right modifier flags and suffix parsing, retained in head hotkey.rs:69–84 and 161–190. Head configuration documentation provides the AltLeft example; the base lacks these options, supporting a new feature.
Changes canonical modifier display from Meta to Cmd. Head still accepts Meta, Cmd, and Command, so no migration requirement or separate user outcome is established.

Parses shortcut keys before configuration merging so equivalent spellings can override or disable defaults. The 0.2.18 base merges raw strings before parsing while documenting Option and Alt as interchangeable, establishing a shipped bug. Tests verify alternate-spelling overrides and disabling; validation improvements are supporting details.

Consumes matching shortcut autorepeats without rerunning commands, as retained in head hotkey.rs:303–307. The released base delegates repeat handling to livesplit-hotkey 0.8.1, whose macOS implementation was not inspected. Whether repeat leakage shipped or arose only in the replacement tap remains unknown.

The merge verifies the integrated left/right modifier implementation and configuration instructions, including leaving the opposite Option key available for typing. Grouped with the feature implementation; incidental dependencies and registration changes receive no separate bullet.

Adds Secure Input detection and change notifications, retained in head session.rs:91–138. Grouped with the warning interface as a diagnostic feature, not a fix for Secure Input itself. Supported-version notification behavior remains a reviewer question.
Extracts shared parachute-image loading. This supports warning and alert changes without providing an independent user-facing outcome.

Adds the warning icon, named menu item, and troubleshooting dialog. Head status.rs:122–132 limits the warning to configurations with key bindings, and status_bar.rs verifies the interface. The base lacks this state, supporting a new diagnostic capability.

Assigns the parachute icon in the shared alert helper, retained in head alert.rs:15–20. The base helper lacks explicit icon assignment. Fullscreen-Space alert behavior was already present and is not claimed as new.
Clarifies that function and page keys use Fn as usual. No bindings, commands, or defaults change, and no new functionality is established.
Changes contributor branch-polishing instructions about backup deletion and reporting old commit IDs. It has no demonstrated application effect.

The merge confirms the Secure Input warning and troubleshooting action remain in head. Head glide.default.toml:54–55 enables the status icon by default. Grouped with the implementation; exact published-release boundary confirmation remains in the reviewer checklist.
Adds a contributor script for checking formatting, builds, and tests in a temporary worktree. The script is absent from the base and does not change Glide behavior.
Adds an agent workflow for reviewing and rewriting development branches. Its skill and interface metadata are contributor tooling, not an application capability.
Changes contributor guidance for splitting capabilities, squashing fixes, and checking commits. These history conventions do not affect released Glide behavior.
The merge is limited to the branch-polishing skill, its metadata, agent guidance, and the validation script. It adds no user-facing application outcome.

Isolates the contributor script's default build output in target/check-each-commit. The affected script was introduced in this range and is absent from the released base, so this is not a shipped application regression.
The merge changes only the contributor script's build-directory behavior already accounted for above. It has no separate user-facing outcome, and the script did not exist at the release base.
